<reason>B built the more coherent cumulative case: the cost-per-contact vs cost-per-resolution frame, the safeguard dilemma (thin protection or savings-eating escalation), and the invisibility of AI failures to the very dashboards A trusted. B won the pressure exchange: it answered A's questions with concrete mechanisms (peak-staffed catch tier, bottom-rung pipeline erosion, all-angry-queue burnout) that A never re-engaged, while A's Q1 answer (repeat-contact tracking) walked straight into B's silent-churn kill. A's baseline reframe ("compared to what?") was genuinely powerful and its structural-savings intuition survived, but A's closing sweep left B's standing cost mechanisms untouched, A never delivered the "not close" math its opening promised, and its opening was clipped. B's closing directly answered A's frame: beating a flawed human baseline isn't the motion, and a ledger structurally blind to its own losses cannot prove savings exceed degradation.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B4.4's silent-churn rebuttal: A's answer that repeat-contact metrics capture "gave up" customers fails because the customer who never returns files no repeat contact — defeating A's pressure-question defense and powering B's closing "blind ledger" inversion of A's no-numbers attack.</best_rebuttal>
